articleTitle: Holographic microscopy. Methods, devices, applications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM'2001. 3rd International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (Cat. No.01EX463)
abstract: The methods of holographic interference microscopy allow one to examine native microobjects in real time, reconstruct three-dimensional images of phase micro-objects, and observe dynamics of their change under influence of various exterior and interior factors. The relative siInplicity and availability of holographic interference methods makes the holographic interference microscope an effective device for various medical examinations. The experimental results on study of blood erythrocytes with the help of a holographic interference microscope are given. The shapes of erythrocytes reflect and affect the physiological state of a human organism. The reconstruction of shapes of blood cells and their change due to various diseases is not only of scientific interest, but also can be a method of effective diagnostics complementing well-known methods of clinical examinations.

articleTitle: Development of IP/WDM optical networks
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM'2001. 3rd International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (Cat. No.01EX463)
abstract: Optical wavelength-routed IP/MPLS networks could be a valid solution in the short time. Optical burst switching may represent an interesting method in the mid/long term. Optical packet switching can be seen as the last step of such an evolutionary path. To achieve satisfactory performance, significant efforts are required in developing key optical devices and components such as semiconductor optical amplifiers, optical gates and space switches, wavelength converters, fast tunable lasers and filters, and wavelength routers. Also some breakthroughs are needed in order to realize mature optical devices which allow dynamic buffering of optical packets.

articleTitle: Two-dimensional Bragg-Ewald's dynamical diffraction and spontaneous gratings
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM'2001. 3rd International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (Cat. No.01EX463)
abstract: Convincing experimental data about a complex spontaneous grating (SG) structure have been revealed under influence of a laser irradiation on thin waveguide photosensitive films. The main features of SG structures are explained in terms of two-dimensional Bragg-Ewald dynamical diffraction (TDDD). A TDDD model is founded on the well-known Sommerfeld's treatment of electromagnetic fields generated by a source near an interface as well as the well-known Ewald's self-consistent principle. TDDD equations turned out to be different in content and form compared to classical Bragg or Rayleigh diffraction on periodical structures.

articleTitle: Surface polaritons minigaps formation for different grating profiles
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM'2001. 3rd International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (Cat. No.01EX463)
abstract: We present investigation of the resonance light diffraction in impedance approximation, both from relief gratings and gratings formed by periodical modulation of the material optic properties. The use of the impedance approximation makes it possible to present results in a rather simple analytical form allowing detailed examination.

articleTitle: Metrology maintenance optic time-domain reflectometers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM'2001. 3rd International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (Cat. No.01EX463)
abstract: Optic time domain reflectometers are intended for measurement of parameters which characterize the radiation spread in a fibre optical line. That is the distance to the place of heterogeneity (damage) in the fibre and also attenuation of optical radiation in optical fibres. The main working principle of an optical time domain reflectometer is determination of optical fibre characteristics by the measured back distance. The main advantage of measurements by the back distance is that they demand access only to one end of fibre link.

articleTitle: Peculiarities of resonance diffraction from periodic structures. Analytical approach
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM'2001. 3rd International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (Cat. No.01EX463)
abstract: An overview in the report of results concerning diffraction by periodic structures under conditions of eigenmodes of the corresponding structure excitation surface polaritons or waveguide modes is presented here. The possibility of detailed analytical investigation of the problem is based upon the restriction with the case of weak scattering. When this restriction is made it is shown that resonance is strong. A simple analytical approach based upon modified perturbation theory allows presentation of results in explicit analytical form. We consider both the simplest geometry case (i.e., the wavevector of the periodic structure is parallel to the plane of incidence) and general geometry, and multiperiodic case, as well. The systematization of the resonances is presented for diffraction from the grating on the surface of high reflecting medium.

articleTitle: Influence of absorption nonuniformity on bolometer surface and its diameter upon a registered focal spot profile
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM'2001. 3rd International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (Cat. No.01EX463)
abstract: We examine the influence of radiation absorption nonuniformity across a surface of cylindrical thin-wire bolometer and its diameter value for registered profiles. We measure the root-mean square radius (second moment) of the sloping incident focused laser radiation. The root-mean square diameter of the focused laser beam is equal to a quadruple value of the second moment of intensity distribution.

articleTitle: Control of transmission in photonic structures with n-i-p-i layers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM'2001. 3rd International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (Cat. No.01EX463)
abstract: Structures with a tunable photonic band gap can be used as effective optical switches. In this paper, the availability of n-i-p-i crystal layers in such periodic structures is considered. The dispersion and transmission characteristics of the GaAs-AlGaAs structures are examined for different excitation levels up to where light amplification occurs, The main feature of the switches is the control of the photonic band gap edge near 1.5 /spl mu/m by light at the shorter wavelengths due to the change in the refraction index of the active layers.

articleTitle: Second-harmonic generation from flashlamp-pumped dye lasers at microseconds pulses
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM'2001. 3rd International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (Cat. No.01EX463)
abstract: A tunable source for UV spectroscopy with 1.5-/spl mu/s pulse duration based on SHG of flash lamp pumped dye laser radiation was developed. The influence of the spatial and spectral characteristics of the laser beam on the efficiency of SHG is determined. We have found that spectral bandwidth should not exceed 0.1 nm, and beam divergence should be at least less than 1 mrad for SHG.

articleTitle: New precise optical powermeter
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM'2001. 3rd International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (Cat. No.01EX463)
abstract: The main components of the optical power meter are photodiode FD (G5832-01); an operational amplifier OA, which converts photocurrent into voltage feedback paths; a multiplexer, which switches feedback paths for automatic change of measurement range; an analog-digital converter which converts amplifier voltage output into digital code; and a microcontroller that is intended for amplification scheme control and also for realization of the function of interface with personal computer. Using a high-sensitivity photodiode allowed us to obtain the required dynamic range of power. The spectral characteristic of this photodiode and calibration factors K were determined from the curve of photodiode spectral sensitivity.

articleTitle: End face nonperpendicularity analysis in fiber connectors
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM'2001. 3rd International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (Cat. No.01EX463)
abstract: High quality fiber optic connectors are a critical element of any fiber optic network. Trapping the bare fiber within a cylindrical ferrule and polishing the end of the fiber-ferrule combination terminate most connectors. The performance of the connectors is determined by a combination of the factors including the fiber size and core centration, the ferrule size, centration and axiality, and the methods used in polishing the fiber during termination. Polishing process forms the end face angle. It is well known, that the polishing technology has influence on return loss. Back reflection or return loss is the amount of light reflected back towards the source relation to the forward signal. Reflection back into a laser cavity can cause result in output fluctuations, mode hopping and a damaged laser. This effect is especially detrimental in high speed and analog applications.

articleTitle: Analytical theory of Wood anomalies under grazing light incidence
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM'2001. 3rd International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (Cat. No.01EX463)
abstract: Although theory of Wood anomalies has a long history, starting from Raleigh's works, the complexity of the problem and wide set of possible applications of corresponding resonance effects (transformation of polarization, specular reflection suppression, energy transformation to waveguide or surface waves, nonlinear surface processes, etc.) in optics, optoelectronics, optical surface and gratings properties measuring, the problem still attracts investigators. The case of grazing incidence on the grating with period d much greater than the light wavelength k which we consider is a specific one because many diffracted waves are close to the plane surface eigenmode (surface polaritons), i.e. we are dealing with multiple linked resonances.

articleTitle: Automated nondestroying roughness control on optical ferrule surfaces
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM'2001. 3rd International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (Cat. No.01EX463)
abstract: In the developed automated quality control system for end face of optical ferrules, a Linnik interferometer scheme, and a CCD coordinate-sensitive photo-receiver are used. There is need to fulfill the following basic requirement in an optical micro-interferometer scheme: the intensity of light flux from standard mirror is approximately equal to light flux intensity from surface of object, because that condition is necessary for interference traces observation. The MII-4 micro-interferometer is intended for end face roughness with greater coefficient of reflection (e.g. metal surfaces).

articleTitle: Features of calculation of wideband dispersion compensator for fiber-optic transmission system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM'2001. 3rd International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (Cat. No.01EX463)
abstract: The aspects of the development of the wideband dispersion compensator on a single-mode optic fibre are considered. The relations, that have to satisfy both the main and compensating fibres so as to provide uniform compensation of chromatic dispersion over a wide waveband while transmitting the multiplex signal, are obtained. The numerical example of the parameters of a fibre for a wideband dispersion compensator is analysed.

articleTitle: Laser magnetic spectroscopy
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM'2001. 3rd International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (Cat. No.01EX463)
abstract: Summary form only given. We discuss transitory laser spectroscopy methods, especially a laser polarimetry method. In details, we discuss detection of weak magnetic susceptibility change.

articleTitle: Modeling of dispersion properties of a Fabry-Perot interferometer by elasticity function
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM'2001. 3rd International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (Cat. No.01EX463)
abstract: Summary form only given. The authors give an optical spectrum simulation result for light reflection from a layered Fabry-Perot interferometer. One can obtain the power reflectance by using Airy's method that traces the reflected waves.

articleTitle: Realization of numerical models for nonlinear impulse interactions in soliton communication lines
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM'2001. 3rd International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (Cat. No.01EX463)
abstract: We consider two methods for analyzing solitons propagation in dispersion-managed communication lines described by nonlinear differential equation. The first method is a split-step Fourier method (SSFM). The second one is the modification of Runge-Kutta-Felberg method (RKF). The obtained results show that SSFM and RKF is a perspective method for a numerical simulation and optimization of high-speed long-distance soliton transmission links.

articleTitle: Sub-wavelength quadratic spatial solitons
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM'2001. 3rd International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (Cat. No.01EX463)
abstract: Summary from only given. Recently attention has been focused on the investigation of nonparaxial optical beams and sub-wavelength spatial solitons that are not satisfied by using a nonlinear Scrodinger's approach. Such solitons can be used for creation of new optical switching devices. The theory of ultra-narrow spatial solitons can be built on Maxwell's equations in a quadratically nonlinear medium. We have investigated nonparaxial narrow quadratic solitons taking into account the effect of nonlinearly induced diffraction, an effect directly stemming from Maxwell's equations and omitted in the paraxial case of wide beams. We have obtained the simple equations for soliton profile envelopes in the planar case and detected the saturation effect limiting the available soliton width from below. This limit is in the order of the linear wavelength and depends on the type of the nonlinear interaction between first and second harmonic waves. We have also found analytically the exact expressions for the fundamental limit of the soliton width and the auto-model profiles of extremely narrow solitons as well as the numeric solutions.

articleTitle: Photonic crystals and photonic microstructures: technologies and device potential
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM'2001. 3rd International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (Cat. No.01EX463)
abstract: My lecture will be concerned with various forms of photonic crystal, but mostly with photonic crystals created by microstructuring techniques and nanotechnology in thin, 'single-mode', optical waveguides. Because of their pre-eminent role in lasers and LEDs, the optical waveguides used for much of the work to be described are epitaxial III-V semiconductor heterostructures. Photonic crystals are interpreted as being regular structures exhibiting a large modulation of the refractive index and with periodicity in one, two or three dimensions. The emphasis in the presentation will be on gaining a physical understanding of how photonic bandgap behaviour can appear in photonic crystals, leading on to various new device concepts. Leading-edge fabrication technology, in particular direct-write electron-beam lithography (EBL) and reactive ion etching (RIE), play an essential role in realising the photonic microstructures which become photonic crystals for light in the near infrared and visible parts of the spectrum.

articleTitle: Planning of SDH system in Ukrainian transmission network
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM'2001. 3rd International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (Cat. No.01EX463)
abstract: After analyzing the modern fiber-optic network constructions in Europe, Japan and USA the all Ukrainian synchronous digital hierarchy (SDH) network project is offered. The problems and prospects of the development of this project are considered.

articleTitle: Simulation of YAG:Nd microchip laser with epitaxial YAG:Cr/sup 4+/ Q-switching layer
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM'2001. 3rd International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (Cat. No.01EX463)
abstract: The microchip Nd:YAG laser Q-switched by the epitaxial film of the Cr/sup 4+/:YAG saturable absorber is considered. The optimal values of the absorber initial transmission and the output mirror reflectivity are being optimized in order to reach the maximum of the energy at the laser pulse.

articleTitle: Peculiarities of light distribution on optical fibre with system of Bragg's gratings
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM'2001. 3rd International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (Cat. No.01EX463)
abstract: Summary form only given. Distribution of light in a single mode fibre with some Bragg's lattices of the same period was analysed by the method of connected waves. With the help of four Bragg's lattices which make up two Fabry-Perot coordinated interferometers an optical fibre spectrometer can be constructed. The scanning process based on a spectral range can be achieved by changing the temperature of fibre. Based on four lattices, which form two Fabry-Perot interferometers operated in real time one can create continual laser radiation in sequenced powerful impulses.

articleTitle: Solution of electromagnetic vector inverse problem of polarimetry for deterministic class of objects on basis of Jones and Mueller matrix formalisms
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM'2001. 3rd International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (Cat. No.01EX463)
abstract: The inverse problem of polarimetry is defined to be the problem of determining the anisotropy and depolarization properties of a studied object, given the probing radiation with definite polarization characteristics and the measured polarization characteristics of scattered radiation. The main subject of this paper is the problem of analysis of information contained in Jones and Mueller-Jones matrices. These matrices provide a complete description of the anisotropy properties of the studied object. However, the information is in the matrix in implicit form.

articleTitle: Trap detectors for power measurements of laser radiation in visible spectral region
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM'2001. 3rd International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (Cat. No.01EX463)
abstract: We present experiments on studying the dependence of the signal of every photodiode at an angle of incidence of its receiving area. The stabilized He-Ne laser having radiation wavelength of 633 nm was used in all the experiments as the source of radiation. While conducting experiments the S1337 photodiode photocurrent change was registered for different angles of incidence (normal, +45 and -45) and states of polarization (s and p) of the registered radiation.

articleTitle: Using of the travelling wave resonator filters for improving characteristics of WDM transmission optical lines
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM'2001. 3rd International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (Cat. No.01EX463)
abstract: The construction and results of accounts of the optical filter consisting of the ring resonator coupled with optical waveguides are submitted in this work. The characteristics of filters for different values of its parameters are represented. The expediency of the application of offered filters in the systems with WDM is marked.

articleTitle: Structure of generalized Mueller matrix including isotropic depolarization
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM'2001. 3rd International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (Cat. No.01EX463)
abstract: Polarization properties of an object in the case of its linear interaction with electromagnetic radiation (frequency of radiation does not change, and object properties are the same in time of interaction) can be described by using 4/spl times/4 Mueller matrix with real elements. For various classes of the objects their Mueller matrices consist of various number of independent elements. The Muller matrix of deterministic class consists of seven independent elements (parameters or freedom degrees) and can be derived from 2/spl times/2 Jones matrix with complex elements transforming electric field components. This matrix has been called pure Mueller or Mueller-Jones matrix. The existence of the only seven independent elements imposes some constraints on inner structure of Mueller-Jones matrix. The main goal of the present paper is the study of the inner symmetric structure of generalized Mueller matrices of these classes of objects and tracing the character of transformation of the previously established Mueller-Jones matrix symmetry structure as a result of taking into account isotropic depolarization.

articleTitle: Simple method of account of dispersion compensator for fiber optical transfer systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM'2001. 3rd International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (Cat. No.01EX463)
abstract: The theoretical principles of a dispersion compensator used in fiber optical lines are given. An explanation of how a dispersion compensator works on dispersion compensated fibre is described. The recommendations for use of this method for compensation in single-channel and WDM systems is given.

articleTitle: Single-mode optical fibers with minimal dispersion and increased effective area
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM'2001. 3rd International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (Cat. No.01EX463)
abstract: The modification of a previously described synthesis method for optical fibres is proposed. Using given values of phase and group velocities of a spreading mode, the method restores a profile of refractive index in a cross section of a fiber. It is shown, that values of group velocities of a spreading mode on a fixed frequency determine completely the changes of the refraction index, and, therefore, a variance of a dispersion in an optical fiber. Single-mode fibers with the enlarged passband, increased effective area and minimal dispersion with wavelength band 1.55-1.625 /spl mu/m are obtained.

articleTitle: Optochemotronics sensors-theory, experiment, practice
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM'2001. 3rd International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (Cat. No.01EX463)
abstract: Chemotronics is concerned with the development of electrochemical devices and sensors. The essence of those devices is applied voltage conversion into an electric current. The electric current flows through an electrochemical cell due to Faraday processes of active substance transformation onto an interface of electrode-electrolyte solution. In contrast to chemotronics optochemotronics is engaged in research and development of different optical devices and sensors, transforming input electrical voltage or current signal into an output optical luminescent signal.

articleTitle: All-optical demultiplexing and format conversion using an ultrafast bistable laser diode
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM'2001. 3rd International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (Cat. No.01EX463)
abstract: All-optical demultiplexing with a signal-bit width conversion function has been experimentally demonstrated using an ultrafast polarization bistable VCSEL. All-optical format conversions (both from RZ to NRZ and vice versa) have also been experimentally demonstrated.

articleTitle: Wave diffraction by semi-infinite periodical structures with axial symmetry
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM'2001. 3rd International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (Cat. No.01EX463)
abstract: A wide range of diffraction wave problem by semi-infinite equidistant succession of identical obstacles with axial symmetry has been considered. The numerical-analytical method decision of this problem solution has been suggested. It is based on the idea of the partial inversion of diffraction problem operator by the following way: the simple part of the semi-infinite obstacle for which the scattering operator is known is extracted. The desired total operator then has been constructed by using specific symmetry of the semi-infinite structure on the basis of the operator mentioned above, which allows taking into account the wave interaction by the obstacle components.

articleTitle: A five-level time-domain model for quantum dot lasers: influence of carrier capture and escape processes on dynamic and static characteristic
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM'2001. 3rd International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (Cat. No.01EX463)
abstract: The model is offered on the basis of the transmission line approach, which allows making researches of dynamic behavior of the quantum dot lasers. The character of the influence of a carrier captures and escapes processes on modulation and current-watt performances are researched numerically. The simulation results indicate, that the greatest influence on the laser performances have the carrier capture processes in quantum dots, and carrier capture from optical confinement layer into the wetting layer. The calculated results have good agreement with experimental data.

articleTitle: Laser beam focal spot analysis
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM'2001. 3rd International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (Cat. No.01EX463)
abstract: Different types of scanners are used now for direct laser beam focal spot measurements: direct with rotated needle and a pinhole and line scanners, as moving slits, knife-edges, and by moving thin wires. With slits and other types of one-dimensional scanners only projections of intensity distributions can be obtained. Threshold for slits is one of the highest. The other way is scanning of a beam by a thin wire when a bolometric signal is measured.

articleTitle: Scattering of laser wave beam on dielectric layer with ferrite film
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM'2001. 3rd International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (Cat. No.01EX463)
abstract: For scattered fields we observed a spatial distribution of one or several laser beams. Our analysis demonstrates a capability to control these characteristics by means of a constant magnetizing field for a wide range. The designed numerical algorithm allows one to carry out computer simulation of pattern and fields for given output characteristics.

articleTitle: Theoretical and experimental researches of thermal deformations in optical resonator elements of lasers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM'2001. 3rd International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (Cat. No.01EX463)
abstract: Summary form only given. The thermal deformations in optical resonator elements of powerful lasers lead to decreasing of resonator stability, to change of spatial parameters of output radiation; and also can cause destruction of optical elements. The results of theoretical researches of temperature fields and deformations depending on the physical characteristics of optical materials, their absorbing ability, and also modes of laser operation are presented in this work. The results of experimental measurements by the interference method of quantity of the thermal deformations in resonator mirrors of powerful lasers are shown. The submitted results allow optimizing parameters of laser resonators for powerful lasers, to prove a choice of optical materials, to simulate the most rational ways a cooling of optical elements.

articleTitle: Diffraction properties of multi-layer holograms
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM'2001. 3rd International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (Cat. No.01EX463)
abstract: Based on the theory of connected waves the peculiarities of diffraction of light on multi-layered holograms was analysed. For two-edged holograms depending on diffraction efficiency from wavelength of the falling light one can observe oscillations, the period of which can be generally determined by the distance between the subholograms. For a multilayered hologram consisting of subholograms depending on the diffraction efficiency from the wavelength only every m-l peak has a big amplitude, the angle's width of this peak and the amplitudes of other peaks decrease with the increase of m. This case represents a multi-layer interferometer. The recording of a multilayered hologram can be done with the help of a simple hologram. Two edged and multilayered holograms as a matter of fact represent indivisible two rays and multi ray interferometers.

articleTitle: Optical induced dynamic nuclei polarization in condensed medias
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM'2001. 3rd International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (Cat. No.01EX463)
abstract: Summary form only given. One of the opportunities of creation of stationary/dynamic (on the contrary static) nuclear polarization (DNP) is represented by multiplexor transitions of electronic pairs is to specify a way of creation and maintenance constant in time of the concentration triplet condition of molecules. Such an opportunity is realized by optical orientation of atoms (molecules) discussed in previous reports. Significant optically induced DNP was observed in solids as well as in liquid solutions. We assume this is due to occurrence of irradiation of triplet electronic conditions or triplet exitons, transitions of relaxation of which in singlet condition on simultaneous superfine interaction is caused by amplification of nuclear polarization.

articleTitle: Modification of synthesis method for effective area singlemode optical fibre optimization
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM'2001. 3rd International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (Cat. No.01EX463)
abstract: The modification of a previously proposed synthesis method is used. A Gel'fand-Levitan mathematical base for solution of the inverse problem of scattering in the non-relativistic quantum mechanic is also used. The law of refractive index profile in the cross-section of synthesized fiber upon its given characteristics is determined. The conditions for definition of spectrum function normalization factors of the synthesized waveguide are modificated. Input data for synthesis are an effective area and phase velocity, or mode field diameter and phase velocity of a fundamental mode of a synthesized fiber. It allows synthesizing single mode optic fibres (SMF) with the increased effective area and mode field diameter. Increasing of an effective area and mode field diameter we can reduce a light intensity in each point and, therefore, decrease nonlinear effects. The effective area characterizes parameter of non-linearity at the description of super short pulses (solitons) propagation in modern fiber optic telecommunication systems. The change of this parameter will allow optimising propagation conditions for solitons.

articleTitle: Many body theory for luminescence in quantum wells
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM'2001. 3rd International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (Cat. No.01EX463)

articleTitle: Model operation of excitation systems of electrodischarge lasers on LC-contour basis by equivalent electrical circuits
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM'2001. 3rd International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (Cat. No.01EX463)
abstract: The excitation systems of an electrodischarge excimer lasers is simulated by a circuit with lumped capacitances and inductances. It is necessary to note, that the excitaion system is usually designed with distributed inductances. Therefore it is expedient to study in more detail the question about the possibility of such model operation. The plan of the excitation system of an electrodischarge laser on the basis of an asymmetrical LC-contour is submitted.

articleTitle: Epitaxial Gd/sub 3/(GaSc)/sub 5/O/sub 12/:Er and CN:Er films in active medium for 1.5-/spl mu/m laser
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM'2001. 3rd International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (Cat. No.01EX463)
abstract: Summary form only given. The studied Gd/sub 3/(Ga/sub 2/Sc)/sub 5/O/sub 12/:Er films were grown using the method of liquid-phase epitaxy on pure Gd/sub 3/Ga/sub 5/O/sub 12/ substrates. The employed films, which differed in the number of Gd/sup 3+/ ions, are replaced by Er/sup 3+/ ions. The Sc/sup 3+/ ions were used to compensate the size of the elementary crystal cell of the film and to bring the size of the elementary cell in correspondence with the size of the substrate. An influence in studied of electromagnetic radiation on epitaxial structure growing processes. High power xenon lamp, pulse and continuous lasers were used in experiments on CN:Er films growing. The model of processes on the crystallization surface is considered and the necessity to take defects kinetics into account when analyzing photostimulated epitaxy is shown. Spectral-luminescent properties of Gd/sub 3/(GaSc)/sub 5/O/sub 12/ and CN films doped with Er/sup 3+/ ions have been studied.

articleTitle: Characteristics of lasers with photonic band gap structures and microcavities
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM'2001. 3rd International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (Cat. No.01EX463)
abstract: Dynamical, threshold current, power versus current and modulation characteristics of semiconductor lasers with photonic band gap structures and microcavities are investigated. Investigations show the possibility of both the output power and modulation bandwidth management by using such structures.

articleTitle: Studies of new dyes for green-blue spectral range of laser action
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM'2001. 3rd International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (Cat. No.01EX463)
abstract: Spectral, fluorescent and lasing properties of a series of benzopyran derivatives were investigated for the purpose of making new active media for flashlamp-pumped dye lasers. The influences of structure changes in this series of the dyes on their spectroscopic characteristics and the laser performance have been analyzed in the work. The fulfilled measurements have shown, that laser efficiency of investigated salts of the benzopyran derivatives exceeds one for their analogue-coumarin 7. Therewithal the compounds, in which molecular structure the free diethylamino group in the 7-th position of the benzopyran nucleus is fixed with two saturated six-membered heterocycles, have the greatest laser output. The results of the work allow developing recommendations for synthesis of new effective laser dyes among compounds of the investigated series.

articleTitle: Application of the ring optical resonators for previous demultiplexing of the signal of HDWDM transmission lines
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM'2001. 3rd International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (Cat. No.01EX463)
abstract: The construction and results of accounts of the optical filter consisting of the ring resonator coupled with optical waveguides are submitted in this work. The characteristics of filters for different values of its parameters are represented. The expediency of application of the offered filters in systems with high density WDM is marked.

articleTitle: Mathematical model of technological CO laser with 20-50 kW power, open contour of work and RF-discharge in supersonic flow
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM'2001. 3rd International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (Cat. No.01EX463)
abstract: The mathematical model of a technological laser with an open work contour and RF-discharge has been developed in a supersonic flow. During the operating time of the CO laser there is a reaction on the catalyst of widely accessible gases: C/sub 3/H/sub 8/ and CO/sub 2/, with subsequent mix by air (up to 90%). The ecological safety of work of the laser is provided at the expense of CO conversion molecules in CO/sub 2/ on the catalyst before emission in an atmosphere. The mathematical model includes an account of process of mixing and reaction of CO/sub 2/ to C/sub 3/H/sub 8/, the mixture with air in the nozzle block, excitation in RF discharge, and processes of conversion CO molecules in CO/sub 2/. The model allows one to account for the parameters and optimisation of the technological laser and RF-discharge in a supersonic flow. The estimation of cost of such a technological laser with capacity of 20-50 kW is at a level of cost of a 1 kW CO/sub 2/ of the laser.

articleTitle: Opportunity of reduction of objects visibility using diffraction-reflecting coverings in conditions of application laser detection systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM'2001. 3rd International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (Cat. No.01EX463)
abstract: We consider a single-channel locator without accumulation of an uninterrupted signal, this is, actually, close enough to a real situation, when the target is immobile and the value of Doppler shift of frequency is given, as far as it is determined by the rate of the movement of the receiving system. Further we use the characteristics of the laser heterodyne locator produced by Rockwell, which has the parameters close to the heterodyne locators of MTL complexes as an example.

articleTitle: Calculation of city synchronous network reliability structure
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM'2001. 3rd International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (Cat. No.01EX463)
abstract: One of the methods of communication networks structural reliability determination is considered. The structure of an actual analog-digital and a projected synchronous Lviv City network was analyzed; percent protection ratio and the methods synchronous network capacity for work recoveries were defined.

articleTitle: Laser beam quality measurements
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM'2001. 3rd International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (Cat. No.01EX463)
abstract: Usually a laser beam is a mixture of Hermite-Gauss or Laguerre-Gauss modes. These beams don't change their shape when propagating through first order optics. Then kurtosis, on-axis intensity, and Strehl ratio will be invariant or dependent on main parameters such as widths and areas. They can be used only for additional characterization or as criteria of noise, high order aberrations, etc. Quality of astigmatic, twisted, partially coherent, and other types of complex beams can be completely described by second order, generalized or power content areas.

articleTitle: Mathematical modeling in measuring methods of optical radiation pulses
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM'2001. 3rd International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (Cat. No.01EX463)
abstract: Methods of mathematical modeling are always used while studying physical processes. Mathematical modeling has appeared to be very useful in the development of measuring devices. Computers are also used for analysis of signals in these cases. This paper proves that mathematical modeling and computer analysis of signals allows one to measure the fast changes of optical radiation power of a thermal receiver, which has a large time constant. The receiver of radiation is a graphite plate with a width of 5 mm. The thermocouples are located on the back surface of the plate. The time constant of the receiver was about 300 sec.

articleTitle: New fissile mediums of tunable lasers on basis of derivative yulolidincoumarine
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM'2001. 3rd International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (Cat. No.01EX463)
abstract: We have studied the influence of the structural and molecular factors of a new derivative of yulolidine on their spectral and generic features in requirements of coherent initiation by excimer XeCl-laser and vacuum-tube pump. The dimensional stabilization of nitrogen atom by yulolidine kern 7-N(CH/sub 2/)/sub 6/ provides a high degree of molecular coplanarity of coumarine. There is a natural bathochromic bias of absorption spectrum and luminescence (on 15-20 nm) and also considerable quantum yield. We have studied the influence of an acid-base equilibrium on spectroscopic and general features of linkage are investigated.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic wave propagation in multilayer dielectric structure containing diffraction grating
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM'2001. 3rd International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (Cat. No.01EX463)
abstract: The numerical code for simulating EH/sub 01/ mode propagation in a structure composed of a dielectric grating placed on a multi-layer substrate is elaborated. The dispersion characteristics, spatial field distribution and dependence of transmission and reflection coefficients via frequency are calculated for different geometrical dimensions of the structure. A method of volume integral equations has been applied. The analytical transformation of integral equations lets us avoid singularities and reduces the problem of integrating to numerical quadrature.

articleTitle: Generation of ultrashort pulses of radiation by dye laser with static DFB
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM'2001. 3rd International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (Cat. No.01EX463)
abstract: We model the generation kinetics for dye lasers with static DFB pumped by nanosecond pulsed radiation. It is shown that such laser generates in the general case a train of pulses of picosecond duration, but under nonhigh excess of pumping threshold-a single ultrashort pulse. The mechanism of generation of USP by the laser with static DFB is due to self-gain-switching, which realized by the generated radiation. In work was searched influence of depth of changing of refraction factor of static DFB and excitement level on generation characteristics of pulses of radiation.

articleTitle: Continuous phase modulation receiver design with artificial neural network
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM'2001. 3rd International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (Cat. No.01EX463)
abstract: The aim of this study is to develop neural network based receiver structures for constant envelope continuous phase modulation (CPM) systems. A feedforward network computation with these back-propagation neural networks was used for this purpose. We present the simulation results of the binary system outputs for the inphase and quadrature components.

articleTitle: Coordinate-free holographic method of determination of polarization characteristics of reflected laser radiation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM'2001. 3rd International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (Cat. No.01EX463)
abstract: We note that photodetectors and recording medium in an optical range detector has an electrical component of an electromagnetic wave of average intensity. That is why for determination of polarization of a reflected wave it is suitable to use Stokes' method. Stokes' method is useful for description of either a completely polarized or partly polarized electromagnetic wave and it is based on measurement of its four characteristics.

articleTitle: Specular diffracted wave polarization control by means of the resonance diffraction
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM'2001. 3rd International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (Cat. No.01EX463)
abstract: We investigate the specular component of polarization at resonance diffraction of an arbitrary polarized radiation from an arbitrary oriented grating. It has been found that the specular reflected wave (that is elliptically polarized in general case) is a nontrivial superposition of the linearly polarized wave (regardless of the incident wave polarization) and the one that corresponds to the reflection from the plane surface with the specific resonance reflection coefficient. This reflection coefficient vanishes for some grating magnitudes.

articleTitle: Frequency noise and spectral spread for semiconductor laser modulated by pseudorandom series of pulses
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM'2001. 3rd International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (Cat. No.01EX463)
abstract: For the first time the results of numerical simulation of the influence of frequency fluctuations on single-mode DFB heterostructure semiconductor laser line shape under pseudorandom pumping current modulation. A new approach is applied for the analysis that has been employed earlier to calculate the dynamics and intensity fluctuations of nearly single mode lasers under pulsed operation.

articleTitle: Mode characteristics of MQW lasers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM'2001. 3rd International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (Cat. No.01EX463)
abstract: Results of investigation of the multiple-quantum well vertical-cavity laser structure including non-uniformity of laser, diffusion processes, dynamical and thermal effects and transparent cavity modes are presented. Obtained results allow optimising lasing properties by changing geometrical parameters.

articleTitle: Modeling excitation system of electrodischarge excimer XeCl-laser
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM'2001. 3rd International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (Cat. No.01EX463)
abstract: In this work a mathematical model of a pumping system LC-circuit was created. This model is based not only on general theoretical positions but also in the same way on experimental dates. The dependence of input energy, efficiency and time form pulse from excitation LC-circuit parameters are investigated theoretically. The common and individual affects of every parameters are established. Two modes of efficient LC-circuit excitation with pumping energy have been theoretically explored.

articleTitle: Atoms' optical orientation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM'2001. 3rd International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (Cat. No.01EX463)
abstract: Summary form only given. We discussed the physical aspects of the atoms' optical orientation (AOO) in gases and vapours; experimental procedure and the possibility of this effect's usage in scientific study. The essence of this exotic phenomenon consists of the following: light with a certain wavelength raises transitions of atoms (usually in transparent gaseous cells) from the basic condition on the nearest excited ones, from which the atoms pass back, letting out quantums of the appropriate frequency. These Zeeman sublevels are split by a weak magnetic field. Experimentally the NMR-absorption by an AOO-system was observed in vapours of many alkaline atoms and isotopes of mercury etc.

articleTitle: Nonlinear anisotropic scattering of laser beam in photosensitive thin AS/sub 2/S/sub 3/-Ag films
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM'2001. 3rd International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (Cat. No.01EX463)
abstract: The photosensitivity of thin As/sub 2/S/sub 3/-Ag films has been known for a long time. However, the nonlinear optical effects developing in these films at large expositions is poorly investigated. The present work is about the inducing of periodical structures (PS) connected with the excitation of waveguide TE- and TM-modes in the film by a focused linearly-polarized Gaussian laser beam. The origin and development of scattering light bands (SLBs) is an external sign of the PS formation. SLBs represent an example of a spatio-temporal transformation of the laser beam in a nonlinear medium.

articleTitle: Application of adaptive methods for increasing efficiency of lidar measurements
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM'2001. 3rd International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (Cat. No.01EX463)
abstract: One of the main difficulties in interpreting of lidar probing results of local space volumes is the presence of the receiving signal parameter fluctuations. These fluctuations are caused by different factors and first of all by the influence of atmosphere turbulence on laser radiation when it is spread over the localized route length. Such influence is known to become apparent in amplitude-phase distortion of optical beam, in reducing coherence and its accidental wandering in space, it results in a considerable quality deterioration of the analyzing information and in decreasing accurate characteristics of the measurement system. Especially this influence is observed with short intervals of detecting reradiated signals and while realizing multiangle sounding ratings, which are typical for the conditions of operative data receiving about the atmosphere characteristics on large space scales.

articleTitle: Undistorted transmission of radiation beams in form of sombrero and super-gaussian functions along hollow-core dielectric waveguides
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM'2001. 3rd International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (Cat. No.01EX463)
abstract: The transmission of the radiation beams with inhomogeneous profile intensity along circular hollow Y-core dielectric waveguides (HDW) is studied in this paper. The numerical method of finding the beam and the waveguide relative parameters for realization of such transmission is fulfilled on the basis of input signal decomposition on the eigenmodes of the HDW. The possibility of undistorted transmission along HDW and the axisymmetrical linearly polarized radiation in the form of the different order sombrero function is shown. Conditions of shaping of the radiation beams having close uniform intensity profile on the output of the HDW at its excitation by quasi-homogeneous radiation are given.

articleTitle: Some features of model operation of electrodischarge excimer lasers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM'2001. 3rd International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (Cat. No.01EX463)
abstract: The original excitation system of an electrodischarge excimer laser on the basis of the LC-generator with two-contour peak capacitance is experimentally implemented and theoretically explored.

articleTitle: Nonstationary processes called of changing work modes in lasers with passive phototropic modulators
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM'2001. 3rd International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (Cat. No.01EX463)
abstract: It's possible to investigate kinetics of lasers with a passive phototropic modulator inside the laser resonator by a system speed equations, which describe temporary change of intensity of radiation, and inversions of active and passive environments. The similar system considers the laser working on the three-level scheme, with a metastable top level.

articleTitle: IP/optical networks: the impact of optical transparency
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM'2001. 3rd International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (Cat. No.01EX463)
abstract: The state-of-the art of transparent optical telecommunication technology is reviewed and possible directions of the future developments are outlined. The fundamentals and results of numerical investigation of the influence of the nonlinear optical phenomena on transmission quality and nonlinear products accumulation in multispan dense wavelength division multiplexed (D-WDM) optical fiber telecommunication systems are reported. Four-wave mixing (FWM), self-phase modulation (SPM), cross-phase modulation (XPM), and stimulated Raman scattering (SRS) phenomena are taken into account. Various types of optical fibers as well as different channel number and channel spacing are taken into account in the analysis.
